Engineering the Shift The Strategic Inflection Engineering the Synergy that Powers Integration Kaynes’ transformation is being built through three connected engines of capability. Each strengthens a critical layer of the electronics value chain. Together, they move the Company beyond assembly into a position of deeper control, higher value capture, and integrated solution delivery. The PCB Advantage Our investments in Tamil Nadu are localising advanced 74-Layer and HDI PCB fabrication, giving us greater control over one of the most supply- constrained layers in high-complexity electronics. By reducing dependence on imported multilayer boards, we are strengthening supply

security, shortening lead times for high- reliability sectors, and capturing greater value at the substrate level. In electronics manufacturing, where substrate availability often determines production schedules, control over this layer creates a structural advantage. Securing the substrate. Strengthening the supply chain. The EMS Engine Our core SMT and box-build expertise continues to serve as the backbone of the Company's execution. This foundation is now being strengthened by the direct integration of HDI PCBs and packaged semiconductor units into our production lines. The result is sharper yield visibility, lower supply fragmentation, and faster time-to-market. What began as a manufacturing

capability is now evolving into a competitive position. Converting capability into execution strength The OSAT Leap Our ₹33,070 Mn facility in Sanand, Gujarat marks our entry into semiconductor Assembly, Testing and Packaging. This milestone has already enabled India’s first commercial Multi-Chip Module. By packaging and validating the core processing components of electronic systems, we are moving from the periphery of semiconductor innovation to a more central role in the value chain. This capability strengthens domestic participation in a layer where India has historically depended on imports. Moving closer to the centre of semiconductor value creation The Integrated Outcome PCB fabrication

gives us control over the substrate. EMS converts that control into reliable production. OSAT brings us closer to semiconductor value creation. Together, these three capabilities create a more integrated, resilient, and value-accretive platform, positioning Kaynes as an Integrated Solutions Architect for the next phase of India’s electronics manufacturing growth. From assembly partner to Integrated Solutions Architect ISM 2.0 Momentum The India Semiconductor Mission (ISM) 2.0 has created a materially de-risked investment environment for semiconductor manufacturing. For our Sanand unit, this is reinforced by 50% central and 20% state fiscal support (on eligible capex of ₹26,150 Mn), strengthening

project viability and long-term confidence. Geopolitical Realignment Global OEMs are diversifying supply chains towards trusted and transparent partners. This positions Kaynes as a credible Indian alternative in an evolving global electronics ecosystem. Accelerated Localisation Demand High-reliability sectors such as electric mobility and railway safety systems increasingly require secure domestic supply chains. This is making local semiconductor and PCB manufacturing not just relevant, but strategically important. Supply Chain Resilience The integration of chip packaging and substrate fabrication reduces exposure to global shortages and supply disruptions. It also enables a more predictable,

Mr. N Chandrasekaran Chairman Dear Shareholders, It is my privilege to present to you the Annual Report of Tata Motors Limited for the financial year ended March 31, 2026 - as a Commercial Vehicles only Company following its successful demerger and public listing on November 12, 2025. This milestone marks a decisive step in our ambition to build a world class commercial mobility enterprise, with strong

leadership in India and a significant presence globally. I would like to thank all colleagues who contributed to the successful execution of the demerger and listing. The year 2026 began with expectations of steady global growth, soft inflation and easier financial conditions. However, the introduction of US tariffs in May 2025 created significant challenges globally. India responded by reducing its GST rates to boost domestic consumption which helped prop up domestic growth rates in the second half of the year. During the year we witnessed positive developments including the signing of the landmark India-EU trade agreement and the interim India-US trade deal. However, by early March, the start

of the West Asia crisis brought rising concerns about stagflation—falling output coupled with rising inflation. Fiscal 2026 Performance In this context, I am pleased to share that your Company delivered a robust performance in FY26. In India, as you are aware, your Company has been the undisputed leader in the Commercial Vehicles market, due to the enduring strength of our brands, the capabilities of our people and customer trust earned over decades. During the year, your Company further consolidated this leadership, driven by focused product interventions, disciplined sales execution and deeper, more meaningful customer engagement, delivering sales volumes of over 4,35,000 vehicles, compared

to ~3,85,000 vehicles in the previous year—representing a robust year on year growth of 13%. This performance was driven by strong momentum across the ‘Intermediate, Light and Medium Vehicle (ILMCV)’ and Small Commercial Vehicles and Pickups (SCVPU) segments. Additionally, we had a notable resurgence in our Heavy Commercial Vehicle (HCV) Segment, which achieved its highest market share to 55% in a decade. Chairman’s Message 8 2nd Integrated Annual Report 2025-26 During the year, your Company recorded its highest ever revenues of H83,855 crore, compared to H76,359 crore in FY25, delivering a robust year on year growth of 9.8%. Profitability strengthened further, with EBITDA margins of 12.3%,

reflecting improved operating leverage and disciplined cost management. The automotive business delivered a return on capital employed of 72.3% among the highest in the global commercial vehicles industry. Collectively, these outcomes highlight the resilience of our business model and our ability to perform consistently across cycles through disciplined execution. The Board of Directors have recommended a final dividend of H4/- per share for Fiscal 26, subject to your approval. Fiscal 2026 Progress Last year, I had shared how your Company had organised itself into eight verticals to create new revenue streams while de-risking the business from economic cycles. I am pleased to report that these

initiatives have translated into strong progress during Fiscal 2026. The 8-vertical structure has enabled sharper focus, accountability and improved performance and improved profitability. Apart from the 4 vehicular segments, we saw strong traction in the other 4 segments Non cyclical segment delivered strong growth of 18.2% with spares and services making a contribution to profitability. TML Smart City Mobility Solutions, with over 3,800 electric buses deployed across 10 cities, surpassed the significant milestone of 50 crore cumulative kilometres while consistently delivering uptime above 95%, demonstrating scale, reliability and impact on urban mobility. Digital platforms continued to scale,

strengthening customer engagement and value delivery. Fleet Edge crossed the milestone of one million connected vehicles while Fleet Verse, our digital commerce platform, recorded robust growth across sales, bookings and enquiries. International Business delivered strong year on year growth of 53.9%, driven by deeper market penetration and notable order wins across Southeast Asia, Africa and the Middle East. During the year, your Company announced the proposed acquisition of the IVECO Group, an important strategic step in our global growth journey. This will bring a strong portfolio of light, medium and heavy commercial vehicles, with operations across European, Latin American and other international

markets, annual sales of approximately ~140,000 vehicles and revenues of €13.4 billion in 2025. This will add scale, complementary markets, strong manufacturing and powertrain capabilities along with a strong technology roadmap aligned to evolving emission norms and alternative fuel powertrains. The year also saw the Company’s continued to focus on renewable energy, circular economy and biodiversity. This year we progressed towards 100% renewable electricity, led the industry’s transition with Battery Electric and Hydrogen trucks and strengthened circularity by bringing several plants closer to Water Neutrality and Zero Waste to Landfill. We also scaled our ProLife and Re.Wi.Re businesses, reinforcing

responsible vehicle lifecycle management, while our biodiversity initiatives - projects in the Central Asian Flyway and Maximus received global recognition. Rooted in Tata Group’s enduring values, our social investments continued to focus on creating sustained, long term impact, benefiting over 2 lakh citizens across 105 districts. With more than 30% of beneficiaries from marginalized communities, these efforts reaffirm our commitment to inclusive and sustainable development, spanning key focus areas such as water conservation, education, skill development and healthcare. Further, our flagship Integrated Village Development Programme (IVDP) has evolved into a scalable model for holistic rural

transformation, now spanning 194 villages across five states. Trends Shaping Mobility Advances in digital technologies and AI are transforming how mobility products are designed, experienced and supported. The transition to clean energy, heightened expectations on safety and the reconfiguration of global supply chains are redefining competitiveness. Geopolitical and uneven economic recovery are adding further complexity, making agility and resilience as critical capabilities. In India, these global shifts are reinforced by strong long-term fundamentals. Sustained investments in infrastructure, logistics modernisation and freight efficiency continue to underpin the relevance of commercial mobility.

Looking Ahead With a strong balance sheet, improving returns and focus on resilience, your Company is well positioned to sustain its profitable growth journey. Our focus will remain on delivering industry leading growth, profitability and returns, supported by a disciplined capital allocation to address emerging mobility trends including digital led solutions, connected vehicle technologies, advanced driver assistance systems, data driven fleet services and new age powertrains—capabilities that will shape the future of safe, efficient and intelligent commercial mobility. Guided by Project Aalingana, the Tata Group’s vision for a greener, cleaner and more equitable future, sustainability is integral

to your Company. The transition to cleaner mobility requires a portfolio of electric, hydrogen and cleaner ICE technologies. While we scale the portfolio of zero emission electric CVs, we will continue to invest in hydrogen-based technologies for heavier-duty segments. On behalf of the Board, I would like to thank the employees, customers, suppliers and shareholders, for your continued trust and support. Warm Regards, N. MD and CEO’s Letter Dear Shareholders, I hope this letter finds you in good health and spirits. FY26 was a defining year for Tata Motors Commercial Vehicles. The successful demerger and listing of the Commercial Vehicles entity marked more than a structural milestone—sharpening strategic intent, strengthening governance and reinforcing a culture of accountability and customer- centric execution. Operating as an independently listed entity is enabling clearer capital allocation choices, faster decision-making and a deeper alignment between strategy and outcomes—true

to our promise of Better Always. I am pleased that our Second Annual Report as a standalone listed Company comes to you at a time when the organisation has emerged stronger on multiple dimensions – financial, operational and organisational. This strength has been built deliberately; with disciplined execution, resilient fundamentals and a clear, action-oriented roadmap for sustainable value creation. I would like to share the progress we made during the year and the principles that will continue to guide us. Industry Context and Our Response FY26 unfolded unevenly for the domestic commercial vehicle industry, with early disruptions muting sentiment before a decisive recovery in the second half.

While external factors such as supply-chain dislocations tested resilience, the industry’s rebound was enabled by structural enablers including GST 2.0 implementation, improving demand fundamentals and rising consumer confidence. Girish Wagh Managing Director and Chief Executive Officer 10 2nd Integrated Annual Report 2025-26 Our focus during this period was not on reacting tactically, but on staying anchored to fundamentals—maintaining execution discipline, protecting customer relationships and aligning supply with evolving demand signals. This approach allowed us to participate meaningfully in the recovery while strengthening our competitive position. Performance Anchored in Execution Discipline

Against this backdrop, Tata Motors Commercial Vehicles delivered 14% (excluding TDM) volume growth in FY26. More importantly, this performance reflected a shift in how we operate—through sharper segment-level strategies, clearly defined customer value propositions and tighter integration between product planning, sales execution and supply- chain readiness. This transformation is translating into stronger customer advocacy, reflected in sustained gains in Net Promoter Scores and overall customer satisfaction parameters. A defining outcome of this approach was the HCV Trucks business achieving its strongest offtake market share in a decade. This was not driven by a single intervention, but by

sustained, insight- led actions—aligning products precisely to duty cycles, tailoring services to address real operating requirements, strengthening consultative selling and engaging customers through deeper insights into their operating economics with Fleet Edge. Towards the end of the year, geopolitical developments in West Asia introduced supply-side disruptions and moderated activity in select sectors. Our response once again underscored how resilience is built—through cross functional coordination across sourcing, manufacturing and sales, calibrated demand-supply alignment and proactive, on-ground customer engagement. Supporting customers through tailored solutions during this period reaffirmed

the robustness of our operating model and the agility of our organisation. Strengthening Financial Fitness Prudently Profitability improvement remained intentional and structured. Rather than pursuing growth for its own sake, we embedded financial fitness into decision-making across the business. Mix improvement, disciplined cost governance and a sharper capital allocation framework ensured that every growth lever was evaluated through the lens of returns and cash generation. Better realisations, rigorous fixed-cost control and a growing contribution from relatively non-cyclical businesses improved the quality of earnings. These were reinforced by systematic working capital discipline and tighter

cash controls across the value chain. As a result, FY26 marked a milestone year—with improved revenues and profits, robust margins and healthy cash flows. These outcomes reflect not only strong market participation, but consistency of execution and the inherent resilience of our business model across cycles. Product Leadership Built Around Customer Economics Product leadership during the year was shaped by a clear conviction: lowering the total cost of ownership across the vehicle lifecycle. Our teams focused on modular platforms to enable speed and scale, strengthened application-led design capabilities and adapted new technologies for Indian operating conditions. The launch of Ace Pro—India’s

most affordable four wheeler mini truck—was anchored in this thinking, addressing the ownership economics of small entrepreneurs and first time business owners. The introduction of 17 next generation trucks and tippers reflected deeper customer co creation and sharper segmentation, setting new benchmarks in safety, efficiency and profitability. A landmark step was the upgrade of truck cabins to meet European safety regulations—a deliberate investment that raises industry standards while strengthening long-term customer trust and brand credibility. Building New Growth Engines with Discipline Beyond core vehicles, we continued to scale adjacencies through a measured, outcome led approach. Parts

and Services sustained their multi year growth trajectory, while new businesses such as Automotive Fluids, Aggregates and FleetCare were scaled with clear customer value and profitability lenses. International Business performance improved through a disciplined focus on local partnerships, tailored products and risk calibrated market expansion across more than 40 countries. Through TML Smart City Mobility Solutions, over 3,800 electric buses were deployed across 10+ cities— enabled by integrated planning covering charging infrastructure, fleet uptime and operational excellence. These deployments illustrate how thoughtful system-level execution translates into dependable public transport and

tangible societal benefits. In the digital domain, FleetEdge— now with over one million connected vehicles—demonstrates the power of data driven value propositions.
